title: ticfac watch: an inline live status for runs, workers, gates, CI and findings
description:
OPERATOR, 2026-09-23: yes to a status view - 'something simple that doesn't assume a pane size. more like advanced interactive cli than full tui'.

SHAPE: INLINE, not full-screen. Bubble Tea in inline mode (no alternate screen, no fixed layout) redraws a status block in place in the normal terminal, reflows to the pane's width, and leaves the final state in scrollback on exit. Lip Gloss for styling; huh for the few prompts. Not a TTY (piped, CI, a log file): plain appended lines, one per change. Built on the cobra + fang command surface (nwj).

WHY, from one day of operating runs by hand (2026-09-22/23): nearly every miss came from running blind - hand-parsing ticfac events JSON; a script (~/.local/bin/pi-follow) to see pi's turns; a watcher that woke only on run end and let remote retries scroll past; stall warnings on the wrong signal read as hangs; close-outs held on CI nobody saw was red, and on 48 untriaged findings nobody saw piling up.

WHAT IT SHOWS, for every run on this machine and in the factory:
  - per run: state, and what it is waiting on (CI, triage, a gate, a person) and since when
  - per tick: try (h58's language), tier and model, executor, elapsed
  - per live worker: its runner's last turns and silence duration (pi-follow built in; the same session log b1t uses for liveness)
  - CI per check per head, including the push/pull_request duplicates close-out reads
  - untriaged findings per epic, with a triage prompt (promote / fixed-as / discard) - the one step that still needs a person until gvc
  - remote retries and interventions, so a flaky connection is visible rather than inferred

It reads only what exists - the run feed and events, attempt records, pi session logs, GitHub check runs, ticfac cloud status - and adds no new source of truth.
acceptance_criteria: ticfac watch renders inline (no alternate screen), reflows to any terminal width and leaves its last state in scrollback; not on a TTY it prints plain appended lines; it shows per run what it waits on, per tick its try, tier, model and elapsed time, per worker its last runner turns and silence, CI per check per head, and untriaged findings with a triage prompt; and it reads only existing records
